sources.title: Build over agreements
sources.verified_claim: Thames Water states planning permission does not grant permission to build over a public sewer; works near mapped public assets can require a separate agreement and exact asset location must be established.

sources.title: Developing over or near sewers
sources.verified_claim: New development near public sewers can require diversion or build-over controls; general distance rules do not prove a candidate intersects a public sewer.

sources.title: Building over sewers or public drains
sources.verified_claim: The regulated process distinguishes sewer sizes, technical review, surveys and final agreement; a project cannot be treated as approved without the site-specific process.

sources.title: Connecting to a sewer
sources.verified_claim: New sewer connections require consent and inspection; a completion certificate confirms only the specific connection work, not general parcel capacity.

sources.title: Working near our pipes
sources.verified_claim: Development near mains and sewers must preserve capacity and maintenance access; exact proximity to candidate land needs asset mapping and project details.

sources.title: Build-over application checklist
sources.verified_claim: A build-over application requires a location plan, drainage plans and foundation relationship to sewers; checklist availability is not a candidate approval.

sources.title: Adopting a sewer
sources.verified_claim: Section 104 adoption follows national Code for Adoption standards and remains the developer's responsibility until actual adoption; an application is not completed adoption.

sources.title: Code for Adoption Agreements consultation on revised panel terms of reference
sources.verified_claim: Ofwat confirms the Code for Adoption Agreements governs agreements between water companies and third parties for adoption of new infrastructure; regulatory framework is not parcel-specific evidence.
